statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-58251: in BusyBox netstat through 1.37.0, a local user can start a network program whose argv[0] contains an ANSI terminal escape sequence, so that a victim who runs netstat -p has their terminal locked up (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2025/04/23/6). The fix passes the program name through printable_string() before printing it (https://lists.busybox.net/pipermail/busybox/2025-August/091698.html). Every DHI busybox package for Alpine 3.23 is built from the source of Alpine's 3.23-stable busybox package at revision 30 (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/3.23-stable/main/busybox/APKBUILD), whose secfixes list CVE-2024-58251 as fixed in 1.37.0-r24 and which applies that patch. Inspected every busybox-source package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository for x86_64 and aarch64: busybox (1.37.0-r30, 1.37.0_git20260210-r31, 1.37.0_git20260212-r31 and 1.37.0_git20260817-r32, plus 1.37.0_git20260210-r30 on aarch64), busybox-static (the same versions plus 1.37.0_git20260209-r31), busybox-extras, busybox-suid, busybox-binsh, ssl_client and the doc, openrc and ifupdown packages. netstat is an applet of /bin/busybox and /bin/busybox.static only; busybox-extras provides network daemons and clients without netstat, and ssl_client and bbsuid are helper programs. Ran netstat -lntp from every published busybox and busybox.static binary against a listening process whose argv[0] contains an escape byte: every one prints that byte as '?'. 1.37.0-r30 is the lowest published version, so with this range every published build is on the fixed side.
